This is a game changer and it’s not predictive - it based on the data … YOUR data. One of my favorite features is the estimated levels of medication in your body throughout the week. Why? This app provides everything you need to understand how your body is reacting to your GLP-1. Just get it. You will be glad you did.

author: Grey's Mom
title: Must for forgetful brains
content:
My ADHD brain can barely remember where I put my something five minutes ago, so trusting myself to remember weekly injections, dose changes, injection sites, side effects, and progress was a bold strategy.

Shotsy keeps track of all of it.

I use it to track my Zepbound injections, and it has become one of the most useful health apps on my phone. I can quickly see when my next shot is due, where I injected last, how different doses affected my progress, and how my weight has trended over time.

The injection site tracking is especially helpful because “I’ll remember where I injected last week” turns out to be a lie I tell myself regularly.

I also love having a place to track side effects and symptoms. When you’re trying to figure out whether a change is related to a dose increase, an injection site, or something completely unrelated, having the history right there is incredibly helpful.

The progress tracking has been motivating too. Instead of obsessing over daily fluctuations, I can see the bigger picture. Since starting Zepbound, I’ve lost nearly 37 pounds, and it’s been helpful to have all of that information organized in one place.

Simple, easy to use, and genuinely useful. I highly recommend it.

author: Playeroo
title: So glad I heard of Shotsy
content:
During my first week on Zepbound I was researching something and I came across a graph that someone posted where they were tracking their progress.  The graph was from Shotsy. I had already been keeping notes on where I was injecting my shots, my weight, the amount of protein I was getting each day (its importance had been highly emphasized), and water intake.  This app seemed to have it all (and more) in one place. But as soon as I saw that after a one week trial I would have to pay, I had my usual reaction - nope. But the more I read about the app, the more I decided it would be worth trying it out.  With what I’m paying out of pocket for Zepbound, the cost is a minimal addition that is making my life much easier!  I will be going for my one month follow up with my doctor next week, and I think the app is going to allow me to show her all of my results and side effects and notes and protein intake, etc. in a very concise way.  
So far I’ve not encountered a single glitch with this app (amazing!). I highly recommend Shotsy to help keep you organized and motivated on your GLP-1 journey.

The efficacy charts and the weight change graph (especially the dosage color coding) make trends really easy to understand at a glance. I also like that it pulls in Apple Health metrics so everything is in one place. When talking with my physician, I can quickly share real data instead of trying to remember details from memory.

My weight bounces a bit, up as much as a pound some days, so it helps to see the long term graph to remember that this is long journey. For example, if I look at the six months I've been doing this, it shows average weight loss is 0.8 lb/week. But if I look at just the last month, as my dose increased, it's 1.2 lb/wk! So this helps me stay the course.

author: LizzrdVanReptile
title: Fantastic comprehensive GLP-1 tracker
content: I wanted a tracker in which to record my weekly injections and track my weights to have all relevant data in one handy place. I looked at a handful of them, but only Shotsy appealed to my nursing sense of documentation and organization. This app gathers the important data involved with GLP-1 therapy - dates, dosages, weights, side effects, and calculates averages based on those data points. It provides a visual graph of weight and also estimates the amount of medication in the body as the week goes on. Practically perfect in every way and well worth the subscription cost. The developer is very responsive and helpful with any issues. The only suggestion I’d offer would be the ability to rearrange sections as desired - between doses, I’d love to have the weight at the top so that I can quickly log daily weights. But that’s a minor tweak, and the app is perfectly functional and useful as is. I’ve recommended to several friends and patients who are on GLP-1 therapy.

title: Great app for tracking GLP-shots and weight
content: This app is really great- I wish it was around when I first started!  I used a spreadsheet I found online to track in the beginning but I switched to shotsy when it was available.  I went back and put in all my data.  It lets you track all the things you’d need- each shot you can put the time, dosage, and a detailed location. The app uses the half life of the med to give you an idea of the levels.  You can also put in your weight each day so that you see a chart of your weight loss. You can also put in your calories and protein if you want.  I also like that there’s a spot for notes each day, so I can put in there if I’m out of town or on vacation or ate a special meal or something.  The one little thing I’ve noticed that is weird is that when you open the app, it can take a bit before your data shows up.  I’m not sure if it’s loading from local storage or the cloud, but a few times I thought the app was stuck only to come back and the data showed up. But overall it’s about the perfect app for a GLP-1 user.

developer_response:
Hi, there was a bug with weight entries in the last version of the app (1.2.8) that should be fixed in version 1.2.9.

After you update, you might still see some lingering issues. If you go to the Shotsy app's "Settings>Apple Health Data>Show All Records" screen (in the app, not the iOS settings), you can delete the most recent weight entry and any duplicate dates that might be there. 

After deleting the most recent entry and any duplicate records, you can re-enter the most recent weight, and that should cause the calculations to be re-run. 

If you still see glitches after this, please get in touch using the Contact Us form in the app's Settings!

I also use the daily notes feature to add detail of any side effects I’m feeling (mine have been very minimal, but it’s nice to have a record in case something I’ve eaten causes the same effect later on).

It’s nice to see the weight loss displayed as a graph line and also shows the total loss from the beginning PLUS the loss for each shot along with the average calories and protein grams for that week. That is really helpful for me so that I can tweak my diet if need be.

I made a suggestion for a possible future enhancement and the developer responded right away, stating it would be added to the list for the team to consider. To me, that shows they really care about making this app the best.

I’ve only been at this a month and I think this app has helped me immensely.

title: Great data visualization, and responsive developer!
content:
Update 8/13/24: 
Amazing - the developer immediately responded to my last review and fixed the issue. So responsive and helpful! Love the data visualization and functionality of this app, absolutely worth the annual cost.  Only one more small picky thing: if developer could fix the today’s data weight input (and other relevant fields) so when you start entering data, it doesn’t add a decimal immediately after the first number input (requiring user to backspace every single time they use this field). I doubt any users have a body weight under 10 lbs ;)

Original review: 
This app is wonderful for what it does. Seriously a great option. Only complaint is that on the main screen, the info from “enter today’s data” (at least the weight info) doesn’t seem to transfer and clear when it’s a new day. I have to go into the calendar page to enter data and have it stay on the correct date. Probably a fairly easy programming issue to fix? author: DreamBelieveAchieve
title: Just What I Needed!
content: My mom takes insulin shots and told me that since I’m taking semaglutide with insulin needles, that I should use a calendar, write down any symptoms and side effects, and write down my injection site rotation. Wouldn’t you know it, there’s an app for that! This app does all of it! I’m able to track my weight, side effects, injection site rotations, and (my favorite part because I’m a science person), it shows you an estimate of how much of the medication is remaining in your system throughout the week. It even gives you a countdown until your next shot and gives you encouraging words once you’ve completed one! I purchased the yearly premium, because I wanted all of the tracking and didn’t find it to be too pricey. Highly recommend!

author: design_grrl
title: Priceless companion for your GLP-1 experience!
content:
I’ve had the good fortune to be a beta tester for Shotsy. Within the first hours of using it, I knew it was an invaluable tool. 

In addition to tracking my shot data—from intervals to side effects to weight loss—it also lets me predict the impact of future titrations and cadence adjustments. 

My favorite feature is the “Shots” view, which overlays your daily “Weight change”, “Average calories/day”, or “Average protein/day” on top of your dose level for each injection. This has helped me see the impact of different titrations on my losses and my diet.

Shotsy is an elegant, easy to use, and powerful companion for your medication!
developer_response: I'm so glad to know it's been useful, thank you!
